sections.title: RAG Quality Engineering: What SF Standards Demand
sections.description: San Francisco's engineering culture has zero tolerance for AI systems that 'kind of work.' ClickMasters builds RAG with the retrieval quality engineering that separates production systems from demos.

items.title: Semantic Chunking
items.description: Documents split at sentence and section boundaries — not fixed character counts — preserving context across chunk boundaries. The single most impactful retrieval quality improvement over naive RAG implementations.
items.label: Chunking

items.title: Hybrid Search
items.description: Combining dense vector search (semantic similarity) with BM25 sparse retrieval (keyword matching) — capturing both conceptual relevance and exact term matches. Critical for technical documentation with precise terminology.
items.label: Hybrid Search

items.title: Cross-Encoder Reranking
items.description: A second-pass relevance model (Cohere Rerank, BGE Reranker) scoring retrieved candidates against the query for relevance beyond cosine similarity. Typically improves answer quality by 15–25% on diverse query distributions.
items.label: Reranking

items.title: Contextual Compression
items.description: Filtering retrieved chunks to the directly relevant passages before generation — reducing prompt token cost and eliminating noise that degrades LLM answer quality.
items.label: Compression

items.title: Evaluation Infrastructure
items.description: RAG evaluation against a representative query set using RAGAS metrics (faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision) — ensuring retrieval quality is measured, not assumed.
items.label: Evaluation

items.question: Can ClickMasters build RAG on GCP/Vertex AI for our SF organization?
items.answer: Yes — Google Vertex AI, Vertex AI Search, and GCP-native embedding models are standard platforms for SF organizations running on Google Cloud.

items.question: How does RAG prevent hallucinated answers from our SF product's AI assistant?
items.answer: Through source-grounding prompts, output validation that checks claims against retrieved documents, and confidence-based routing for uncertain responses. RAG dramatically reduces hallucination by grounding answers in actual retrieved content.

items.question: Can RAG integrate with our Notion, Confluence, or internal wiki?
items.answer: Yes — ClickMasters builds document loaders for Notion, Confluence, SharePoint, Google Drive, and other common SF tech company knowledge management platforms.

items.question: How long does RAG development take for a San Francisco SaaS company?
items.answer: 8–20 weeks for most SaaS RAG features. Multi-tenant enterprise RAG platforms: 12–24 weeks.

items.question: What vector database does ClickMasters recommend for SF applications?
items.answer: Pinecone for fully managed production scale; Weaviate for organizations wanting more control; pgvector for teams with existing PostgreSQL infrastructure. ClickMasters evaluates based on your scale, team, and cost requirements.

items.question: Do we retain full ownership of our RAG system after ClickMasters builds it?
items.answer: Yes — complete IP transfer at project close including vector store configuration, ingestion pipelines, prompt templates, and application code.
